newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says it will intervene to defend peso.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says it will intervene to defend peso.

text.p: The Philippine Monetary Board said on Wednesday it would continue with its market-determined exchange rate policy and intervene strongly to maintain an orderly currency market.

"The (Central Bank) will intervene strongly using all its available policy weapons to maintain an orderly foreign exchange market and to penalise speculators," the Monetary Board said in a statement following a regular meeting.
The Monetary Board is the highest policy-making body of the Central Bank and is chaired by Bank Governor Gabriel Singson.
"The country's current flexible and market-determined exchange rate policy will be continued," it said in a statement.

The comments come after a fresh attack on the peso, sparked by a Singapore newspaper report that Manila was discussing a possible devaluation. The Central Bank was forced to intervene heavily to defend the peso following the report.
The Monetary Board said its exchange rate policy had allowed the country to strengthen its external balance of payments position over time and respond to unforeseen shocks in a timely manner.
It noted that first quarter GNP was a strong 6.1 percent, inflation had fallen to 4.6 percent in the first half of the year while exports in January-May were up 123 percent.
